0.title: By Rules
0.content: The By Rules tab applies filter rule sets with AND and OR conditions. Choose whether to search the Whole Model, Current Selection, or Active Space.

2.title: Rule Sets
2.content: One rule set is created by default. You can edit it or create additional rule sets. | Click New to create a rule set. Double-click a rule set to rename it. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. | Select a rule set and click Duplicate. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. | Select a rule set and click Remove. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. | . Use the search box to find rule sets.

3.title: Definition
3.content: This tab allows you to create specific filter conditions for each rule. For this, select a rule from the table above to allow you to edit the filter settings. | Open the first drop-down list and choose Object Types. | Select the second drop-down list to choose the properties of the selected objects. | Choose the Condition to apply filter. | Enter a value or select a suggested value from the drop-down list. | . Click Filter to run the condition rule. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Add condition . You can also apply more conditions to your rule. Click Add to insert a new definition into your rule, following the “AND/OR” condition. Note that if you select the rule created and click Add, you will add a new definition as a child, thus creating a tree structure for your rule. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Remove . Select the conditions created and click the Remove button to delete them. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Search . Use the search box to find filtered elements in the main table. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Select . Select the filtered elements with the checkboxes, then click Select to select them in the view. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Isolate Objects . Select the filtered elements with the checkboxes, then click Isolate to isolate them in the view. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Click End Isolation or use the AutoCAD UNISOLATE command to return to the entire model view.

4.title: Profile
4.content: Create profiles to save the rules and conditions created to filter the model in AutoCAD. Creating Profiles . OneFilter profiles make it easy to save your settings and reuse them later. It is also a handy way for BIM Managers to create standard rules (e.g., filename conventions) and share them across the organization. | Click on the Profile drop-down list. | Click on Add New, and enter a Profile name. | Click to save the profile. | . The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. BIM managers can create profiles in a shared network location so users can import the same rules. See Importing Profiles. Export Profile . OneFilter profiles make it easy to export profiles to stay compliant with your company standards (e.g., profiles in a network location). | Click on the Profile drop-down list and click to export. | Use the Windows File Explorer to select a folder to save the profile (e.g., in a shared folder, network location, or local computer). | Click on the “Save” button to export the profile. | . The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Importing Profiles . OneFilter profiles make it easy to import existing profiles to stay compliant with your company standards (e.g., profiles in a network location). | Click on the Profile drop-down list and click to import. | Use the Windows File Explorer to find the profile (e.g., in a shared folder, network location, or local computer) | Click on the “Open” button to import the profile. | . The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Deleting Profiles . | Click on the Profile drop-down list. | Click on the Delete icon next to the profiles list. | Confirm. | . The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD.

7.title: Simple
7.content: The Simple tab filters objects and layers, and lets you refine the results by property. | Select whether to filter the Whole Model, the Current Selection, or Active Space. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. | Activate the Objects and Layers table with the switch in the table header. | Select the objects or layers to filter. The matching elements appear in the table on the right. Use the search box to find objects and layers. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. | .

8.title: Filter by Property
8.content: Refine the selected objects or layers by choosing a property, condition, and value. | Open the first selection list and choose a property. | Open the second list and choose a condition. | Enter or select a property value, then click Filter. Click Clear to reset the property filter. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. | . Search . Use the search box to find filtered elements in the main table. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Select . Select elements with the checkboxes, then click Select to select them in the view. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Isolate Objects . Select elements with the checkboxes, then click Isolate to isolate them in the view. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD. Click End Isolation or use the AutoCAD UNISOLATE command to return to the full model view. Reset . Click Reset to clear the filtered elements. The image may show an earlier version of OneFilter for AutoCAD.

15.title: Install
15.content: Compatibility . | Windows 7, 8, 10, and 11. | AutoCAD 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, and 2027. | . Standard Installation . This method is ideal for individuals who want to install DiRootsOne on one computer. | Run the DiRootsOne installer. | Select the AutoCAD versions and click Install. | Wait for the installation to complete and click Finish. | . Silent Installation . This method is ideal for IT administrators who want to deploy DiRootsOne to multiple computers. In these commands, // is replaced by the installer with the MSI package path. Place MSI options and properties after it. | Install for all compatible AutoCAD versions: . <installer-name>.exe /i // /qn accept_eula=1 . | Exclude specific AutoCAD versions. This example excludes AutoCAD 2021, 2022, and 2023: . <installer-name>.exe /i // /qn accept_eula=1 autocad2021="" autocad2022="" autocad2023="" . | .

16.title: Uninstall
16.content: Using the installer user interface . | Run the DiRootsOne installer. | Select the AutoCAD versions and click Remove. | Wait for the uninstallation to complete and click Finish. | . Using the installer silently . Uninstall DiRootsOne without user interaction. The // marker is replaced with the MSI package path: . <installer-name>.exe /x // /qn . From the Control Panel . | In the taskbar search box, type Control Panel and open it. | Select Programs > Programs and Features. | Right-click the program you want to remove and select Uninstall or Uninstall/Change, then follow the prompts. | .

17.title: Updates
17.content: DiRootsOne includes an updater that checks for new versions when AutoCAD closes. It lets you install the update or be reminded the next day. Updater Settings . You can adjust the update check frequency (two days by default) and the download folder. Automatic update checks can’t be disabled in the user interface. You can reduce how often they run by setting the check frequency to 365 days. IT administrators can change the update check frequency in the updater configuration file. | Go to %programdata%\DiRoots.DiRootsOne\Settings. | Open updater.ini. | Find CheckFrequency=2 and change the value, for example, to 365. | . We recommend keeping DiRootsOne up to date. Support is not provided for outdated versions.

22.title: Table of contents
22.content: . | TOC | . Just the Docs uses lunr.js to add a client-side search interface powered by a JSON index that Jekyll generates. All search results are shown in an auto-complete style interface (there is no search results page). By default, all generated HTML pages are indexed using the following data points: . | Page title | Page content | Page URL | .

23.title: Enable search in configuration
23.content: In your site’s _config.yml, enable search: . # Enable or disable the site search # Supports true (default) or false search_enabled: true . Search granularity . Pages are split into sections that can be searched individually. The sections are defined by the headings on the page. Each section is displayed in a separate search result. # Split pages into sections that can be searched individually # Supports 1 - 6, default: 2 search.heading_level: 2 . Search previews . A search result can contain previews that show where the search words are found in the specific section. # Maximum amount of previews per search result # Default: 3 search.previews: 3 # Maximum amount of words to display before a matched word in the preview # Default: 5 search.preview_words_before: 5 # Maximum amount of words to display after a matched word in the preview # Default: 10 search.preview_words_after: 10 . Search tokenizer . The default is for hyphens to separate tokens in search terms: gem-based is equivalent to gem based, matching either word. To allow search for hyphenated words: . # Set the search token separator # Default: /[\s\-/]+/ # Example: enable support for hyphenated search words search.tokenizer_separator: /[\s/]+/ . Display URL in search results . # Display the relative url in search results # Supports true (default) or false search.rel_url: false . Display search button . The search button displays in the bottom right corner of the screen and triggers the search input when clicked. # Enable or disable the search button that appears in the bottom right corner of every page # Supports true or false (default) search.button: true .

24.title: Hiding pages from search
24.content: Sometimes you might have a page that you don’t want to be indexed for the search nor to show up in search results, e.g, a 404 page. To exclude a page from search, add the search_exclude: true parameter to the page’s YAML front matter: . Example . --- layout: default title: Page not found nav_exclude: true search_exclude: true --- .

25.title: Generate search index when used as a gem
25.content: If you use Just the Docs as a remote theme, you do not need the following steps. If you use the theme as a gem, you must initialize the search by running this rake command that comes with just-the-docs: . $ bundle exec just-the-docs rake search:init . This command creates the assets/js/zzzz-search-data.json file that Jekyll uses to create your search index. Alternatively, you can create the file manually with this content.
